privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.body: {site} stores your email address and a hashed password so you can sign in, plus what you choose to post: your username, bio, profile picture, ratings, reviews, comments, likes, follows, lists and compounds. Your username, bio, picture and everything you post are public, visible to anyone whether or not they are signed in, while your email address is never shown to other users. We use only the cookies needed to keep you signed in, your theme and search language are saved in your browser, and there are no ads. To understand how the site is used, we record which pages are visited and actions like signing up, logging an item or following someone. These are linked to your account when you are signed in, never include anything you write, and set no cookies. Your data is processed by Supabase (database and storage), Vercel (hosting), Resend (sign-up and password-reset emails) and PostHog (usage analytics), and item titles, descriptions and pictures come from Wikipedia and Wikimedia Commons, which are contacted when an item is looked up. What you type into search goes directly from your browser to Wikipedia, so the Wikimedia Foundation receives your search terms and IP address. You can delete your account and everything you have posted at any time from Settings, and for anything else, including requests to see or correct your data, write to {email}.

guide.thatSAboutTheOnly: That’s about the only suggestion I can think of. This is of little importance to you, but I designed this site with two obsessive user-archetypes in mind, namely those of the Diarist and of the Codifier.
guide.theDiaristChronicallyAppraisesExperience: The Diarist chronically appraises experience. They log “Hello (Salutation)” quite soon after having greeted someone. To the Diarist, items are instances. “Hello (Salutation)” will be logged approximately 4,000 times over the course of a decade. The Diarist, holidaying in Italy, crouches over a Lenovo Trackpad to give Italy 3-and-a-half stars. Perhaps a meandering journal entry is written. One could imagine the Diarist combing through a recursively shortened moment, never quite managing to log everything in it.
guide.theCodifierIsMoreConcerned: The Codifier is more concerned with the imposition of a kind of order on the world. Perhaps they’d simply like to make a novel observation about every given thing, or rank all 7,500 edible apple varieties in descending order, taking rigorous taste notes for each. The Codifier thinks of items not as instances, but as representatives for a larger class of objects. Unlike the Diarist, they have little to say about themselves. Their satisfaction lies in an interminable but concrete sense of progression.
guide.neitherOfThesePeopleExist: Neither of these people exist, and even these brief descriptions overlap somewhat. I just like websites that I can lose myself to completely for no reason, and it’s fun to imagine characters undertaking Borgesian tasks on mine. Have your fun.
guide.welcome: Welcome to {site}. On here, you can review anything that has a Wikipedia article. The articles themselves aren’t displayed, so I suggest (gently) that you review the concepts themselves, rather than their associated Wikipedia pages. You can also make ranked or unranked lists of these concepts.
